source_findings: Only torque_allocator.c is compiled. Snapshot exactly torque_allocator.c, torque_allocator.h and torque_contract.h. No other native unit, probe or Python controller is compiled or linked.

The producer exports tc_allocator_version, tc_allocator_abi_sizeof and tc_allocate_propulsive_torque. It uses fixed-size tagged records and four abstract slots, ordinary automatic arrays/scalars, no heap, runtime IO or persistent state.

Arithmetic includes binary64 division by converted active-count, additions, subtractions, ordered comparisons, epsilon 1e-12 and status threshold 1e-9. The explicit ordered four-slot total is retained. Strict static assertions and no-fast-math guards remain byte-exact.

torque_contract.h supplies data definitions; this allocator source calls no external tc_* function. Do not copy the guard annex's tc_validate_allocation/tc_contract_reason unresolved-symbol prediction. Math classification, C memory/string routines and ABI/compiler helpers are observed from actual objects; no exact symbol list or costs are predicted.
Numeric contract2, shared ABI1 and allocator version1 remain unchanged. Object generation does not check round-to-nearest, subnormal retention, overflow behavior or parity at runtime on Cortex-M4.

The reviewed normalized offline producer remains a candidate only. The existing validation/base guard/pedal/clock/final gate remains necessary; no transport, signal ownership, physical motor mapping or control-policy change is introduced.

exact_execution_contract: Final protocol-v1 must first be committed on a new branch from the exact approved base. Driver implementation and actual tools are separate later stages; current workspace proposal is not authorization to run them.

Implement a separate additive driver with frozen protocol/source/header/helper hashes and exact flags/order, tool allowlist and four-row/31-command denominator. No direct shell, linker, script wrapper, implicit installed compiler, source rewrite, ARM executor or emulator.

Create one new attempt at workspace work/enme408-allocator-cortex-m4-v1 only if absent. Reject existing files/directories, symlink destinations and overlap in either direction with the whole checkout, source, archive, toolchain or prior attempts. Do not create inside any retained attempt (ancestor receipt.json). Resolve canonical paths, including Windows aliases, before containment checks; source snapshot contains exactly the three pinned ordinary files.

Save preparing receipt and exact protocol, executed driver, executed unchanged helper and native snapshot before verification. Preexisting historical file bindings are checked before any new executable and after finalization. Preserve raw Git/local line-ending identity separately where applicable; exact .c/.h bytes and normalized hashes are both recorded.

Fresh verify the archive/tree/all five tools first. Use unchanged clean_environment, then locally remove DEBUGINFOD_URLS and set no toolchain/global environment variables. Every objdump invocation also has explicit --no-debuginfod. No implicit source/debug lookup or network dependency is requested.

Run all commands serially from the exact native snapshot. Actual argv and canonical cwd are recorded before subprocess launch; use a fixed 60-second per-command timeout, captured raw stdout/stderr with hash/path, actual return code or launch/timeout error and elapsed wall time. No timing value is interpreted as target latency.

Version and multilib failures stop. Ordinary compile or inspection/metadata failures mark that row failed and preserve its outputs; continue the remaining frozen rows where safe. Unexpected source/tool/integrity/IO/launch/timeout failure stops conservatively with not-run rows explicit. Never backfill missing calls or replace the planned denominator by the completed count.

Only compilation uses -c. No additional preprocessing, optimization search, alternative flag probes, new source unit or automatic retries. If a disassembler option/format is rejected or an instruction is unknown, retain the failure; any adjusted protocol/driver and distinct attempt require a visible separately reviewed amendment.

After the attempt rehash source/snapshot/protocol/helper/driver, all used tool/header dependencies and historical anchors/cohorts. Do not silently pass a drifted attempt. Record four individual row outcomes, actual command count, two ABI-specific repeat comparisons, all failures and no-target-execution fact.

metadata_and_acceptance.elf: Use raw bytes plus llvm-readobj logs: ELF32 little-endian ARM relocatable, complete bounded section table and ARM.attributes. Retain actual e_flags and all AEABI tags rather than fabricating a platform wire ABI.

aeabi_policy.interpretation: Same reviewed ARMv7E-M/M-profile/Thumb2, VFPv4-D16 and single-precision-permission metadata checks as old helper. These express compiler settings/ABI attributes, not measured FP execution, target numeric behavior or compatibility with an unidentified team firmware.

metadata_and_acceptance.sections: Retain every section record, full Berkeley and SysV size logs and ELF file length. Reconcile parsed Berkeley fields with actual logs and distinguish code/constants/data/BSS, relocations/unwind/debug/attribute metadata. No linked flash/RAM fit threshold or summing separate units into a firmware size claim.
metadata_and_acceptance.symbols: Retain raw complete symbol/relocation log and undefined nm names. Check all three public allocator definitions exist in the actual symbol table; extra compiler-local definitions are recorded. No exact helper-name allowlist or assumed helper performance/availability. Do not predict guard-unit tc_* references for this source.
metadata_and_acceptance.disassembly: Retain raw llvm-objdump executable-section disassembly with addresses, instruction bytes, function labels and relocations. Require output contains the three public allocator symbol labels and nonempty disassembly; flag any <unknown> instruction as a retained metadata diagnostic/failure. Thumb triple and Cortex-M4 CPU are explicit. Literal data/mapping symbols and relocation placeholders are not executed opcodes or resolved call targets. Do not infer instruction count, branch-path cost, WCET, software-library parity or complete call graph from this listing.
metadata_and_acceptance.local_stack: Retain every emitted .su record/qualifier with actual file hash. Use unchanged parser: missing .su is explicitly not_emitted, not zero stack; this means local-frame evidence is unavailable and must be visible. Numeric frames exclude caller/callee/compiler helpers, interrupts, scheduler and FPU context. No whole-call-stack or budget assertion.
metadata_and_acceptance.dependencies: Preserve literal Windows drive backslashes, escaped spaces and continuations via the reviewed lexer; canonical roots via reviewed alias repair. Retain .d bytes/hash and every dependency identity; each resolved dependency is in the exact native snapshot or fully verified toolchain. Any external/missing/changed dependency fails integrity.
metadata_and_acceptance.repeats: Compare SHA256 of repeat1 vs repeat2 objects separately for hard and softfp, requiring all corresponding rows pass. Record full object bytes/hash. Equality means reproducible bytes only under these exact frozen conditions; no cross-ABI equality or timing claim is required.

limitations: The exact team STM32 part, ABI, compiler/library/startup configuration, flash/RAM budgets and task/deadline/recovery ownership remain unknown; these candidates do not select them.

This compiles one producer unit into relocatables. It neither links all five units nor supplies/reset/startup/HAL/interrupt/controller scheduling/physical signals. Unresolved helpers may dominate linked size, numerical behavior or execution cost.

Clang static assertions and strict flags constrain translation; generated Cortex-M4 code has not been executed. Host bit-parity and sanitizers remain prior host evidence, not target parity or safety certification.

Binary64 arithmetic, ordinary rounding/subnormal retention and source epsilon quirks remain unchanged. Single-precision FPU metadata and an assembly listing cannot establish correct target runtime behavior of double operations.

No target/HIL/emulation, firmware image, CAN/transport, flashing, motor mapping/calibration/traction policy, real hardware actuation, whole-stack/resource-fit/deadline/WCET or independent shutdown authority.
